unresolvedReferences.description: Heading lists 惟正 (Weizheng) though English calls all three sons; Weizheng is not among the seven sons in s0032-s0038.
English 'Mizhou' for 沔州 (Mianzhou).
English calls 義武 a temple name; it is a posthumous name.
Death at 49 follows the guimao (1243) appointment but is not explicitly dated; age claim not encoded.
English 'Jiazhou' for 嘉川.
English 'Kuixia Gorge' for 夔峽.
Wang Dechen's death at 36 is undated in the text (during the Diaoyu siege, historically 1259).
English calls 忠烈 a temple name; it is a posthumous name.
English 'grand preceptor' for 大司徒 (Grand Minister of Education).
English 'Kang Tuhu' for 康土禿 and 'Zhu Qisun' for 朱禩孫 (Zhu Sisun).
三年 read as Zhongtong 3 (1262) continuing from s0120; 四年春 as 1263.
Emperor's 汝立利州之功 rendered 'you won Lizhou'.
Alantai'er/Hunduhai = Alandar and Qongdaqai, Ariq Böke's commanders; Kublai's accession (1260) not dated in text.
惟某: one son's name is lost; not extracted as a person.
English calls 忠惠 a temple name; it is a posthumous name. 儀同三司 rendered 'minister-of-state rank'.
English 'pacification commissioner of Shaanxi' for 陝西等處行中書省平章政事 (manager of governmental affairs).
English 'pacification commissioner of Yunnan' for 雲南諸路行省平章政事.
English 'Golden Spear Guard' for 金吾衛.
Wang Weizheng's death at 44 follows the Zhiyuan 22 (1285) appointment but is not explicitly dated.
Song commander 何統制 (He) has surname only; not extracted.
Prince Shou (壽王), an imperial nephew, is not further identified.
The Prince of Anxi's consort and Weizheng's mother are unnamed.
